fatal_blockers: The passing flag certifies only the preregistered q=3,m=8 sample. It provides no asymptotic NO lower bound, polynomial-size reduction, NCP hardness, or CVP hardness, and the packet correctly contains none that can be promoted.

The claimed collision mechanism is not sound for the linearized code: the all-eight and twisted-holonomy checks exhibit illegal affine combinations whose entire walk shell cancels. Thus collisions in an underlying cover do not imply shell weight for arbitrary mixed words, which are the words soundness must control.

The proposed simple-path mutation has a direct padding obstruction. Take a fixed bounded-degree NO 3DM component with a weight-q0+2 odd cover and append arbitrarily many disjoint YES components; the resulting NO witness has only O(1) activated simple paths while its original weight and the YES baseline grow linearly, so the ratio tends to one.

Replacing walks by simple paths therefore removes the repeated-cycle amplification without supplying global collision expansion. A q=4 sweep cannot escape this obstruction or prove a polynomial path count for logarithmic path length.

The current finite gain may be duplicate-coordinate replication: indexed nonbacktracking walks retain multiplicity even when they induce the same Boolean monomial and can repeatedly traverse a constant collision cycle. No evidence separates this effect from genuine global soundness.
evidence: Machine verification exactly supports the bounded figures: primary length 4 has worst tested YES 3, best tested NO 33, nominal length 1277, ratio 11, and the reported finite exponent 0.3352636.

The verifier enumerates the spans of the tested lifted fibers, but its success predicate checks only YES=3, sampled NO>5, and improvement over the finite baseline. It contains no assertion quantifying over growing instances.
The hostile reports give illegal shell-free words of original/total costs 6 and 9. These agree with STATUS, IDEAS, NOTES, and proof_cvp.md, all of which explicitly deny asymptotic promotion.

The source itself gives walk count m times roughly Delta^(r-1); no bounded-occurrence reduction or asymptotic degree/path theorem is supplied. The proposed q=4 experiment is absent from the verifier evidence.
